title: The balance sheet does not balance
meaning: Total assets differ from equity plus liabilities by more than a thousandth of total assets, in the figures the filing itself states for its own period end.
remedy: Read the statement of financial position in the report. A difference of this size is usually a tag with the wrong scale or a line tagged twice rather than an error in the accounts.

title: Total assets are not the two halves added up
meaning: Total assets differ from current plus non-current assets by more than a thousandth of total assets.
remedy: Read the asset side of the statement. IAS 1 lets an issuer present assets in order of liquidity instead, in which case the two subtotals mean something else and the check does not apply.

title: Revenue less cost of sales is not the gross profit
meaning: Revenue less the cost of sales differs from the gross profit the filing states by more than a thousandth of revenue.
remedy: Read the income statement. An issuer presenting by nature rather than by function has no cost of sales line, and a filing that tags one anyway is tagging something else with it.

title: The result before tax less the tax is not the result
meaning: The result before tax less the income tax expense differs from the profit or loss by more than a thousandth of revenue.
remedy: Read the income statement. The result of the discontinued operations falls between the two lines and is added back by the check where the issuer tags it; a difference that remains is a line the check does not know about.

title: The three cash flows do not add up to the movement in cash
meaning: The operating, investing and financing cash flows do not sum to the movement in cash and cash equivalents, by more than a thousandth of total assets.
remedy: Read the cash flow statement. The effect of exchange rate movements on cash held is presented separately and is the usual explanation.

title: A period ends before it begins
meaning: A fact of the filing carries a period whose first day is after its last.
remedy: The fact is wrong as published. Read it in the viewer of the repository, which shows the context the issuer tagged.

title: Total assets are negative
meaning: The filing states a negative figure for total assets, which no statement of financial position can show.
remedy: Almost always a sign tagged onto a figure that is already positive. Read the statement.

title: A fact carries neither a number nor a text
meaning: A fact of the filing has no value and no text, so it says nothing at all.
remedy: Nothing can be read from the fact. It points at a defect in the filing or in the repository's conversion of it.

title: One figure tagged twice with two values
meaning: The same concept, period, unit and breakdown is tagged more than once in the filing with values that differ. Tagging it twice with the same value is ordinary -- a figure appears in the statements and again in the notes -- and is not reported.
remedy: Read both facts in the viewer. Which of the two a reader should use cannot be decided from the data, so neither is dropped.

title: One concept in two units in one filing
meaning: The filing tags the same concept in two different units, such as a figure in two currencies, outside any breakdown that would explain it.
remedy: Read the facts. A presentation currency and a functional currency both tagged under one concept is the usual cause, and the figures are not comparable with one another.

title: A period ends after the filing was processed
meaning: A fact reports on a period ending after the day the repository last processed the filing.
remedy: A forward-looking figure in the notes is a legitimate cause; a year mistyped in the context is the other.

title: The repository's own validation found errors
meaning: The repository reports one or more validation errors against the filing. The count is the repository's and nothing here re-ran its rules.
remedy: Read the validation report at the repository. An error there does not mean a figure is wrong, but it does mean the filing does not meet the format.

title: No total assets tagged
meaning: The filing tags no total assets for its own period end, under any of the concepts this check looks for.
remedy: Read the statement of financial position: the line is almost certainly there, tagged with a concept of the issuer's own making, which the comparison cannot use.

title: No revenue tagged
meaning: The filing tags no revenue for its own financial year, under any of the concepts this check looks for.
remedy: Read the income statement. An issuer whose revenue is interest income tags it elsewhere, which is the ordinary case for a bank.

title: No result for the year tagged
meaning: The filing tags no profit or loss for its own financial year.
remedy: Read the income statement. The line is required, so its absence points at a tag the comparison does not know rather than at a report without a result.

title: The same period filed more than once in one language
meaning: The issuer has more than one filing for the same period end in the same language, both carrying facts.
remedy: Ordinarily a correction. The later filing by the day the repository processed it is the one to read, and both are kept.

title: A filing with no facts
meaning: The repository lists the filing but publishes no xBRL-JSON for it, so it contributes nothing to the table of facts.
remedy: Nothing to do here. It is counted so that a population can be read as what was filed rather than as what could be parsed.

title: Most figures tagged with the issuer's own concepts
meaning: More than half the numeric facts of the filing are tagged under concepts the issuer created rather than concepts of the taxonomy.
remedy: Nothing is wrong with the filing. It says how far its figures can be set beside another issuer's, which is the thing an extension-heavy report makes hard.

title: The balance sheet does not balance
meaning: Total assets differ from total liabilities plus stockholders' equity by more than a thousandth of total assets, in the figures the report states for its own period end.
remedy: Read the balance sheet. A difference of this size is usually a tag with the wrong scale or a subtotal tagged with the wrong concept.

title: The two totals of the balance sheet differ
meaning: Total assets differ from the total of liabilities and equity the report states under its own concept, by more than a thousandth of total assets.
remedy: Read the balance sheet. The two lines face each other on the page and are equal by construction, so a difference is a tagging fault.

title: Revenue less the cost of revenue is not the gross profit
meaning: Revenue less the cost of revenue differs from the gross profit the report states by more than a thousandth of revenue.
remedy: Read the statement of operations. A registrant that presents no gross profit line is not checked; one that presents it and fails this is tagging one of the three with the wrong concept.

title: Income before tax less the tax is not the net income
meaning: Income before income tax less the income tax expense differs from the net income by more than a thousandth of revenue.
remedy: Read the statement of operations. The discontinued operations are added back by the check where the registrant tags them; equity method earnings presented after tax are the other line that falls between the two.

title: The three cash flows do not add up to the movement in cash
meaning: The operating, investing and financing cash flows do not sum to the change in cash the report states, by more than a thousandth of total assets.
remedy: Read the cash flow statement. The effect of exchange rates on cash held is presented separately and is the usual explanation.

title: A period ends before it begins
meaning: A fact of the filing carries a period whose first day is after its last.
remedy: The fact is wrong as published by the Commission. Read the filing itself on EDGAR.

title: Total assets are negative
meaning: The filing states a negative figure for total assets, which no balance sheet can show.
remedy: Almost always a sign tagged onto a figure that is already positive. Read the balance sheet.

title: The filing was made before the period it reports on ended
meaning: The day the filing was made is earlier than the last day of the period it reports on.
remedy: Read the filing. The period end of a filing is the latest period any of its facts reports on, so a fact looking forward -- a share repurchase settling next quarter, a payment falling due -- carries it past the day the filing was made. The filing is then sound and the period end derived for it is not the period it is about.

title: No total assets tagged
meaning: The annual report tags no total assets for its own period end.
remedy: Read the balance sheet. The line is required of every filer, so its absence points at the company file rather than at the report.

title: No revenue tagged
meaning: The annual report tags no revenue for its own financial year, under any of the concepts this check looks for.
remedy: Read the statement of operations. A registrant whose revenue is interest or premium income tags it elsewhere, which is the ordinary case for a bank or an insurer.

title: No net income tagged
meaning: The annual report tags no net income for its own financial year.
remedy: Read the statement of operations. The line is required, so its absence points at a tag the comparison does not know.

title: One figure tagged twice with two values
meaning: The same concept, period and unit is tagged more than once within one filing with values that differ. The same value twice is ordinary and is not reported.
remedy: Read the filing on EDGAR. Which of the two a reader should use cannot be decided from the company file, so neither is dropped.

title: One concept in two units in one filing
meaning: The filing tags the same concept in two different units, such as a figure in two currencies.
remedy: Read the facts. A presentation and a functional currency tagged under one concept is the usual cause, and the figures are not comparable.

title: A later report states a different figure for the same period
meaning: An annual report filed later states a figure for the same concept and period that differs from the one the period's own report stated, by more than a hundredth of it. Share counts and per-share amounts are passed over, a split restating those by arithmetic rather than by judgement. A company file carries every filing's account of every period, which is what makes this visible at all.
remedy: Read both filings. A restatement, a reclassification and a correction all look like this, and which it is cannot be read from the figures alone. The esef module has no counterpart to this check, the repository publishing each filing separately.

title: The fiscal year on the cover does not fit the period end
meaning: The fiscal year the cover page states is more than one year away from the calendar year the reported period ends in.
remedy: Read the cover page. A registrant whose financial year ends in January names it by the later year, which this check allows for; a greater gap is a tagging fault.

title: The framework the filing reports under cannot be told
meaning: The filing tags against neither the US GAAP nor the IFRS taxonomy, so nothing says which framework its figures were prepared under.
remedy: Nothing is wrong with the filing. A report that tags only cover-page facts is the ordinary cause, and its figures are not comparable with either framework's.
